solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One insect with indistinct back devouring another

indicators.note: one piece eating another means it is placed around it
back says the word for indistinct is read the other way round

explanation.surface: One bug, blurred at the rear, gobbles up a second bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the dim word to give MID, and 'devouring' wraps it round the second insect; 'One insect' is the definition, 'another' the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantid, or praying mantis, is a single predatory insect.

clue.text: Is this writer ready to be a chum abroad?

parts.note: turned into a question about the setter: am I
go as in all systems go, meaning ready

explanation.surface: The setter wonders whether he is prepared to be a pal while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer' is the setter, so 'Is this writer' becomes AM I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, so a pal in foreign parts.

clue.text: Lifetime appears to be so 'growth-restricted'

parts.note: a tree's years show as rings or lines in its trunk, and a road bordered by trees is edged, or restricted, by growth

explanation.walkthrough: Two cryptic hints: a tree's age is recorded in lines, and 'growth-restricted' describes an avenue bounded by trees.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue with trees along both sides is bounded by vegetation on each edge.

clue.text: Around end of the month there's the same again

indicators.note: the word for the same goes around the other letters

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, the same

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: As the month closes, the same thing happens yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' is ditto, shortened as in lists; 'Around' wraps it about the final letter picked by 'end of' and the month's short form.
explanation.definitionFit: De novo is Latin for afresh, from the beginning once more.

clue.text: Engineer needing heather and bits of twigs etc for building

definitions.text: bits of twigs etc for building

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam engine fame
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A builder needs heather and twigs to put up a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle work is interwoven sticks and twigs used in building walls and fences.

clue.text: Whatever dear Tom messed up, it's all forgotten now, buddy!

indicators.note: messed up says the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone reassures their friend Tom that whatever he bungled is now past.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a past matter that can no longer be changed, so best forgotten.

clue.text: Maybe drops of tea for those rested up hiding pain

indicators.note: hiding means the outer word conceals the pain word within it
up in a down clue reads the word for rested from bottom to top

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Little sips of tea served to people who are resting, concealing an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the rested word bottom to top, giving TAS, which 'hiding' wraps round the pain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea tastings are small samples sipped to judge the brew, examples of the definition.

clue.text: Sort of image shining at top of house

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the other

explanation.surface: A picture glinting at the top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho is a lithograph, a print made from a flat stone or plate.

clue.text: Few nest or fly in national park

indicators.note: fly suggests the letters scatter like birds leaving

explanation.surface: Few birds nest or fly about in this protected area.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest in Hampshire, southern England, is a protected national park of woodland and heath.

clue.text: Dislikes crossing the swirling brine and hides away

indicators.note: crossing means the outer word spans the other letters
swirling churns up the letters of brine

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes sailing over the rough sea goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges the sea water to give IBERN, which 'crossing' puts inside the dislike word.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that hibernates retreats to sleep through winter out of sight.

clue.text: Competitor's aim putting off international community

indicators.note: putting off means one letter is discarded

explanation.surface: A contestant's goal discouraging the global community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting off' removes I from TO WIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a settled community of people, larger than a village.

clue.text: Thoroughly impress girlfriend from the East End?

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End

explanation.surface: Wanting to dazzle a girl from London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is an idiom for overwhelming or amazing them.

clue.text: Lousy type in party place, half cut, rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over flips the combined letters end to end
half cut keeps only the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A disreputable sort at a party venue, half drunk, tumbling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' trims POSITION to POSI; DO + POSI is read backwards by 'rolling over'. 'Lousy' means of the louse kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice belong to the crustacean order Isopoda, so an isopod is a louse-like creature.

clue.text: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city

definitions.text: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city

parts.words: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city
parts.note: put the letter A before this bird's name and you get a Nile city near the great dam

explanation.walkthrough: The Egyptian city's name is A followed by the bird, so the bird is seen in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a large white long-necked waterfowl found on rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Sweeping tricky spot, glide along audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the words are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: a hole is a tricky spot, and to sail is to glide along

explanation.surface: Smooth gliding past a difficult patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale changes are sweeping, far-reaching and indiscriminate.

clue.text: Devious excursions made by very good stars crossing area

indicators.note: crossing has the two letters straddle the area letter

parts.note: Aries is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: Wanderings by an excellent group of stars over a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are erratic wanderings or whims, from Latin vagari, to roam.

clue.text: More than one coward eats words with soldiers invading

indicators.note: invading puts the soldiers inside the other word

parts.note: one who eats his words recants

explanation.surface: A man retracts his statement as troops invade.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreants are cowardly or faithless people, a plural noun.

clue.text: Going down suddenly in brawl when gold has been stolen

indicators.note: has been stolen means that piece is removed

explanation.surface: Plunging into a fight once the gold is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Free fall is an uncontrolled drop under gravity, a rapid descent.

clue.text: 'Edgy' sort, having to exist without system, runs

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for exist surrounds the system word

explanation.surface: A nervous person who must live without structure keeps running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the exist word surrounds the system word; 'Edgy' hints at an edge, not nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderer lives on a frontier, the edge of a country, hence an edge dweller.

clue.text: Garment is said to offer such shelter

indicators.note: is said to means it sounds like the word for garment

explanation.surface: An item of clothing claims to give a certain protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cote is a small shed for birds or animals, such as a dovecote.

clue.text: A mother has order put in for a plant

indicators.note: put in places the order letters within the mother word

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A mum orders something for her garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Amomum is a genus of aromatic plants of the ginger family, including cardamom.

clue.text: Female free from danger initially hidden in grass

indicators.note: initially hidden means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to rescue is to free from danger

explanation.surface: A woman saved from peril was at first concealed in tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a common tufted pasture and lawn grass.

clue.text: Somerset town affected by fire according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as it sounds when spoken

explanation.surface: A news report says a West Country town was damaged by fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Frustrated head losing heart with introduction of current measure

indicators.note: introduction of means the measure is inserted
losing heart drops the middle letters of head

parts.note: the ampere is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: A boss lost courage when a new power metric came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves HD from the head word, and 'with introduction of' slips the unit of current between those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hampered is being hindered or impeded, a synonym for being thwarted.

clue.text: Develop as devil, twisted at the outset

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters is swapped round, the first moving one place on

parts.note: deuce is an old word for the devil, as in what the deuce

explanation.surface: Growing into a devil, warped from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted at the outset' swaps the first two letters of DEUCE, D moving after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or bring forth something latent.

clue.text: Star group of 15 meeting a divine incarnation

parts.note: 15-across ends in Aries, the constellation of the ram

explanation.surface: A constellation meeting a god in human form.
explanation.definitionFit: Rama is the seventh avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu.

clue.text: Being pot-bellied, it's a bit of a game boarding a vehicle

indicators.note: boarding puts the game piece inside the vehicle

parts.note: a domino is a piece from the game of dominoes

explanation.surface: A paunchy person playing a board game on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominous means having a large belly, from abdomen.

clue.text: Writer, mostly boring, has hesitation to become a swinger

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter

explanation.surface: A dull, faltering author turns into a party animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro, so literally one that swings.

clue.text: Clare's place won't need new inspection

indicators.note: won't need means a letter is dropped

parts.note: County Clare lies in Munster, an Irish province

explanation.surface: Clare's home won't require a fresh check.
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is an assembly of troops for inspection or roll-call.
